summary: Anna Filigenzi works in archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A member of the Italian Institute for Africa and the East (1984) and director of the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003), she held posts at Naples "L'Orientale" and Federico II.

Anna Halafoff specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned a BA from the University of Melbourne, a Master of Letters from the University of New England, and a PhD from Monash University, and holds a post at Deakin University.

Anna Kamensky (1867–1952) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at the Bestuzhev Courses and earned her PhD from the University of Geneva in 1926, where she taught comparative religion as privatdozent from circa 1928 to 1950.

Anna Kramskova specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She earned her master's degree at Saint Petersburg State University (2014–2016) and served as a research assistant at the Institute of Linguistic Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 2019.
Anna M. Shields is a sinologist who taught at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) before becoming a professor at Princeton University in 2015.

Anna Sawerthal is a Tibetologist who completed an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, with instruction from Johanna Buß, Dawa Tsering, and Norbu Tashi. She earned her PhD from Heidelberg University.
Anna Scarabel is an Indologist who earned her PhD from Heidelberg University in 2018 and is attested as a faculty member at the University of Vienna in 2026.

Anna Seidel (1938–1991) was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated in Munich and Hamburg, she studied under Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. She served at the EFEO and Institut du Hōbōgirin, and founded Cahiers d'Extrême-Asie.

Anna Stirr is an Indologist who earned a BA from Lawrence University (2002) and a PhD from Columbia University (2009). She held posts at The New School, Oxford, and Leiden, and joined the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 2012.

Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (PhD ~1987). She worked at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (~1976–1990) and UCLA (~1990–1998) before becoming professor of linguistics at NYU (~1998).
Anna Šebestová specialized in linguistics and Indology. She earned her PhD at Charles University in 1919 under the supervision of Josef Zubatý.

Anna-Pya Sjödin is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Uppsala University in 2007, supervised by Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, having also studied with Barbro Eriksson.
Annarao Kulkarni works in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held positions at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Anncharlott Eschmann (1941–1977) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She studied at Munich, Marburg, and Heidelberg University, where she earned her PhD in 1969 and served as an assistant in 1975.
Anne Burchardi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Erik Haarh and has held a post at the National Museum of Denmark.

Anne Carolyn Klein works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia (PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins), she trained under numerous Tibetan masters, became a professor at Rice University, and co-founded the Dawn Mountain Center.

Anne E. Monius (1964–2019) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Harvard under Diana L. Eck and Kausalya Hart, she taught at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) and became professor of South Asian Religions at Harvard in 2002.

Anne Feldhaus is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Manhattanville University and earned her doctorate from the University of Pennsylvania in 1976, later becoming Distinguished Foundation Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University in 1981.

Anne Hardgrove is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Carleton College and the University of Michigan, taking up a post in history at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.

Anne Hopkins Aitken (1911–1994) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Scripps College, Northwestern, Stanford, and Oxford. She co-founded the Honolulu Diamond Sangha in 1959 and the Maui Zendo.
